title: ‘Blood in a dish’ to test and fix rare diseases at their source   | WEHI
summary:
Researchers will develop a new gene therapy platform designed to correct hundreds of rare blood and immune disorders caused by single-letter DNA mutations, thanks to a $5 million Medical Research Future Fund grant.

More than 600 distinct blood and immune diseases are caused by tiny errors in the genetic code within blood stem cells. These conditions are rare but often severe and life-limiting, and collectively affect millions of people worldwide.

title: Boy with rare condition amazes doctors after world-first gene therapy | BBC News | Project Alive
summary: Three-year-old Oliver Chu has astounded doctors with his progress after becoming the first person in the world with his devastating disease to receive a ground-breaking gene therapy. "Every time we talk about it, I want to cry because it's just so amazing," says the boy’s mother, Jingru. He has a rare, inherited condition called Hunter syndrome - or MPSII - which causes progressive damage to the body and brain. In the most severe cases, patients with the disease usually die before the age of 20.
